tool.name: ThermoRawFileParser
tool.description: Parses a Thermo RAW file containing mass spectra to an open file format
tool.command: ThermoRawFileParser.sh -i '$raw_input' -b output_file -f $output_format #if $gzip_output --gzip #end if #if $metadata_options.output_metadata --metadata='$metadata_options.metadata_format' #end if #if $advanced.ms_level --msLevel $advanced.ms_level #end if #if $advanced.collision_energy --ignoreInstrumentErrors #end if

param.name: raw_input
param.label: Thermo RAW File
param.help: Thermo Fisher RAW file containing mass spectrometry data

param.name: gzip_output
param.label: Compress Output with gzip
param.help: Enable gzip compression for output files

param.name: output_metadata
param.label: Output Metadata
param.help: Generate metadata file alongside converted spectra

param.name: ms_level
param.label: MS Level Filter
param.help: Only output spectra from specific MS level

param.name: collision_energy
param.label: Ignore Instrument Errors
param.help: Continue conversion even if instrument errors are encountered

tool.help:
**What it does**
ThermoRawFileParser converts Thermo Fisher RAW files to open mass spectrometry formats. This is the first critical step in creating vendor-independent, reproducible LC-MS workflows.
The tool uses the official ThermoFisher ThermoRawFileReader library, wrapped to run on Linux with Mono, ensuring accurate and complete conversion of vendor data.
**Supported Output Formats**
- **mzML**: HUPO-PSI standard format (recommended for most workflows) - **Indexed mzML**: mzML with indexing for faster random access - **MGF**: Mascot Generic Format (for search engines) - **Apache Parquet**: Columnar storage format (for big data analysis)
**Inputs**
- **Thermo RAW File**: Raw mass spectrometry data from Thermo Fisher instruments (.raw or .RAW extension)
**Options**
- **Output Format**: Choose between mzML, MGF, or Parquet formats - **Gzip Compression**: Reduce file size (recommended for large datasets) - **Metadata**: Export instrument and acquisition metadata separately - **MS Level Filter**: Extract only MS1, MS2, or MS3 spectra - **Error Handling**: Continue conversion even if instrument errors are present
**Outputs**
- **Converted Spectra**: Mass spectra in selected open format - **Metadata** (optional): Instrument and acquisition parameters
**Use Cases**
1. **DDA Workflows**: RAW → mzML → peptide search → protein identification 2. **DIA Workflows**: RAW → mzML → DIA-NN → peptide quantification 3. **Metabolomics**: RAW → mzML → XCMS → metabolite detection 4. **Data Archiving**: Convert proprietary RAW to open mzML for long-term storage
**Performance Notes**
- Conversion time: ~1-5 minutes per RAW file (depends on size and MS levels) - Memory: <4GB for typical files - Gzip compression reduces file size by 50-70% - Indexed mzML provides 10-100x faster random access
**Why ThermoRawFileParser?**
- **Open Source**: Apache license, fully transparent conversion - **Linux Compatible**: Runs on any platform (vs Windows-only MSConvert) - **Official Library**: Uses ThermoFisher's own reader for accuracy - **Container Ready**: Easy deployment in workflows and pipelines
**Citation**
If you use this tool, please cite:
Hulstaert N, Shofstahl J, Sachsenberg T, et al. ThermoRawFileParser: Modular, Scalable, and Cross-Platform RAW File Conversion. J Proteome Res. 2020 Jan 3;19(1):537-542. doi: 10.1021/acs.jproteome.9b00328
**More Information**
- Homepage: https://github.com/compomics/ThermoRawFileParser - Documentation: https://github.com/compomics/ThermoRawFileParser/blob/master/README.md
